finding_key: packages/backend/src/datasource/datasource.service.ts::ssrf / internal port scanning: user-supplied host+port are connected to with no allowlist, and raw driver errors are returned to the caller, making the backend an oracle for the internal network
evidence: Verified against the supplied files: CreateDataSourceDto only length/range-validates host and port with no address denylist, and createClient (datasource.service.ts, the `new Client({ host: ds.host, port: ds.port, ... })` block the diff touches to add `types`) dials whatever the user supplies. testConnection returns `{ success: false, error: (error as Error).message }` and executeQuery rethrows `pgError.message` in a BadRequestException, so raw driver errors (ECONNREFUSED vs. timeout vs. protocol error) do reach the authenticated caller — a working internal port-scan oracle, exactly as claimed. The claim misreads nothing; my only qualifications are that the routes are gated by JwtAuthGuard plus workspaceService.assertMember (so it is not unauthenticated), and that this is entirely pre-existing and inherent to a user-configured Postgres connector, with the leak limited to connection-level signals rather than response bodies. Hence real, but I rate it minor.
